title: Affective drivers of generative AI acceptance in higher education: a UTAUT extension across on-campus and distance learning
author: Mareike Mueller, Evelyn Kaestner
description: Purpose This study aims to examine the drivers of students’ intention to intensify generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use in higher education, focusing on the incremental explanatory value of Affective Evaluation and differences between on-campus and distance-learning students. Design/methodology/approach Building on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), the study analyzes survey data from 502 students at a German university of applied sciences. Hierarchical regression analyses, group comparisons and moderation analyses are used to examine predictor–intention relationships and the role of study mode. Findings The UTAUT-based model explained approximately 62% of the variance in Intention to Intensify GenAI Use. Affective Evaluation contributed significant incremental explanatory power and showed the largest standardized coefficient, alongside significant effects of Performance Expectancy and Social Influence. Distance-learning students reported higher intention than on-campus students, although the effect was small. title: Understanding the potential role of GenAI and knowledge governance in the higher education sector through knowledge governance theory
author: Xie Xiaojuan, Muhammad Azfar Anwar
description: Purpose This study aims to investigate how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) knowledge workflow capabilities influence community knowledge governance (CKG) and community knowledge sharing (CKS) within higher education communities, through the mediating mechanisms of knowledge digitization and knowledge legitimacy. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 357 faculty members, postgraduate researchers and academic staff operating within higher education institutions actively integrating GenAI tools into their academic knowledge workflows. WarpPLS structural equation modeling was used for model analysis, enabling simultaneous assessment of direct and indirect effects across the proposed framework. Scales were adapted from validated instruments in prior knowledge management, AI capability and academic behavior research, ensuring reliability and construct validity across all measured variables. author: Leonardo Henrique Brandão-Monteiro
description: The following chapter derives from research shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic. Although its main aim was not to discuss the impacts of the pandemic, the context in which it occurred allows us to ask: what do the changes brought about by pandemic-related restrictions reveal about the social mediations of our participants’ out-of-school study practices? To address this question, we employed a theory-generating methodology, supported by questionnaires that provided contextual elements of these practices and by explicitation interviews that allowed a deeper analysis. These interviews provide the main data analyzed. Tim Ingold’s concept of enskillment and Bernard Charlot’s concept of the relationship with knowledge structured the analyses conducted. The data originate from a comparative study involving three California universities and one Brazilian public university. We argue that the main issue faced by the U.S. interviewees was de-enskillment, a broadening of the Ingoldian concept. Meanwhile, among the Brazilian participants, it was possible to shed light on inequalities between public high school students and private high school attendees. title: From Ideation to Implementation
publisher: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
author: Brad Ost, Bryan A. Briones
description: This chapter examines how the Atlanta University Center Robert W. Woodruff Library developed an AI Sandbox to support responsible, equitable, and innovative adoption of generative AI across its three Historically Black Colleges and Universities consortial partner campuses; Clark Atlanta University, Morehouse College and Spelman College. Framed within the evolving and expanding role of academic libraries, it confirms that libraries are uniquely situated to address the challenges of AI access, data privacy, governance, and information literacy while also advancing research, teaching innovation, and student success. The chapter traces the sandbox's conceptualization, partnership development, governance structuring, environmental scanning, and strategic planning, highlighting some examples of lessons learned throughout the process. It demonstrates how the AI Sandbox enhanced the AUC Woodruff Library's mission by linking emerging technologies with existing research support, digital scholarship, and ethical information practices to create a sustainable model for AI-enabled scholarship.

title: Critical Thinking in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
publisher: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
author: avram anderson, Ahmed Alwan
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has had and will continue to have, an unprecedented impact on higher education. Yet the integration of AI literacy into postsecondary curricula remains rare and inconsistent. Academic librarians, due to their expertise in information literacy and interdisciplinary collaboration, are uniquely positioned to address this gap. This chapter presents a case study of a credit-bearing AI literacy course housed within the academic library at CSUN. The course was designed not only to introduce students to AI but to support the development of epistemic agency, allowing them to critically evaluate AI-generated information, interrogate algorithmic bias, and navigate an AI-mediated information environment. Grounded in the UNESCO AI Competency Framework for Students, the Council of Europe's three-dimensional model of AI literacy and ACRL Framework for Information Literacy for Higher Education, the course emphasizes the practical and human dimensions of AI literacy and provides a pedagogical framework that academic librarians can adapt across instructional formats.

description: Teachers and curriculum writers in Chinese foreign language education have used the label AI-enabled production-oriented approach (AI-POA) for several years, but it has no agreed definition, dimensions or boundary, and studies that appear to address the same arrangement cannot be compared. This paper treats the difficulty as conceptual. A systematic search of 1,373 records from OpenAlex and four from a targeted Chinese search yielded 46 studies published between 2017 and 2026, coded for design, technology role, POA stage and outcome. The corpus is deliberately mixed and is not a set of 46 instances: eight are POA sources written before generative tools existed, twenty-six combine POA with AI, ten examine AI in second language reading without POA, and two are reviews. title: Reclaiming the Civic Mission of Higher Education Through Social Entrepreneurship and Experiential Assessment
author: Sein Tin, Lachhuman Gurung
description: Higher education is facing a compounding legitimacy crisis driven by neoliberal marketisation, generative artificial intelligence, and public doubt about the value of degrees. This chapter argues that assessment is a significant yet underexplored mechanism through which neoliberal values are reproduced: standardised, output-driven individual assessment narrows curricula, marginalises civic and ethical learning, and reinforces educational inequalities, while AI exposes the limitations of these models. In response, the chapter develops the Civic-Embedded Assessment Framework (CEAF), grounded in civic university, experiential learning, student integration, and social entrepreneurship theories. The CEAF proposes four interdependent pillars: social value creation, authentic knowledge application, community engagement, and student identity development. Using a conceptual, practice-informed methodology, the chapter illustrates the framework through three cases, including a community football tournament planned, delivered, and evaluated by mixed undergraduate cohorts in partnership with a local charity, with a post-event evaluation serving as the summative assessment. title: AI-Augmented Research Support for Commerce Collections
publisher: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
author: Deepak D.
description: This chapter analyses a case study of the systematic use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in re-engineering the research-support service for its commerce collection in an Indian management institute library. The study follows the evolution of a library from reactive support via reference work to proactive, data-driven research partnership based on a single-site case-study design across two academic years: 2023-24 and 2024-25. The five-layer AI tool stack—presentation, AI service, knowledge, infrastructure and governance—is introduced alongside a six-step augmented research workflow using generative AI assistants, retrieval-augmented chatbots, automated summarisation of results, citation bots for tutorial creation and text-mining services.The use of pre- and post-implementation usage data, qualitative feedback, and an adoption-maturity model illustrates measurable improvements in discovery efficiency, citation accuracy, and faculty research output.

title: Inner Development Goals and Collective Social-Emotional Health in Higher Education Institutions
publisher: Cultivating Collective Socio-Emotional Well-Being in Organizations
author: Yuliya Shtaltovna
description: This chapter examines collective socio-emotional health through the lens of the Inner Development Goals (IDG). Moving beyond individual resilience, it argues that socio-emotional health is an organizational capability shaped by relational infrastructure, leadership norms, communication cultures, institutional practices, and technological conditions. The chapter positions the IDG dimensions of Being, Thinking, Relating, Collaborating, and Acting as a framework for understanding how inner capacities become collective practices that support trust, psychological safety, empathy, shared meaning, and responsible action. Drawing on selected IDG cases from the Casebook of IDG Implementation into Higher Education, it illustrates how relational well-being can be intentionally designed in higher education organizations and communities. The chapter offers recommendations for researchers, educators, leaders, policy makers, social innovators, and well-being professionals seeking to cultivate emotionally healthy collectives in an age of complexity, artificial intelligence, and human sustainability.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Journalism
publisher: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
author: Andleeb Raza, Rahul Kumar
description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping journalism through automated content creation, data analysis, and personalized news distribution. While it enhances efficiency, AI also raises profound ethical concerns, including algorithmic bias, deepfake-driven misinformation, and the erosion of editorial accountability. This chapter explores AI's dual impact, emphasizing how algorithmic gatekeeping and synthetic media threaten media literacy and democratic discourse. Case studies illustrate how filter bubbles and computational propaganda exploit AI to distort public perception. A pilot study in Jammu and Kashmir reveals high media literacy among youth (mean: 3.98/5), despite regional vulnerabilities, demonstrating education's vital role in building resilience. The chapter advocates for comprehensive media literacy programs, regulatory frameworks to ensure algorithmic transparency, and newsroom policies that maintain human oversight. Addressing these challenges is essential to harness AI's potential while safeguarding journalism's integrity and democratic values in digital landscape.

title: The emotional labor of AI integration: a constructivist grounded theory study of academic librarians' work with generative AI tools
author: Akinade Adebowale Adewojo
description: Purpose This study examines how academic librarians in Nigeria experience and manage emotional labor when they integrate generative artificial intelligence (AI) into reference services, and how that labor is carried out through epistemic work. Design/methodology/approach A constructivist grounded theory study was conducted in three academic libraries (federal, state and private) in Kwara State, Nigeria. Twenty-one reference, liaison and systems librarians took part through semi-structured interviews, non-participant observation of AI-mediated reference consultations and artifact analysis. Data were analyzed through initial and focused coding, constant comparison and memo writing. Findings Reference librarians' anxiety centered on professional credibility, liaison librarians' on bias in AI outputs and systems librarians' on technical instability. Librarians managed these feelings through two forms of epistemic work: epistemic vigilance, the alertness that sets how closely an output is checked, and epistemic stewardship, the verification and correction done to protect patrons. author: Alicia Mwami, Raymond Ndomba
description: This study examined the influence of teachers’ access to Information and Communication Technology (ICT) facilities on students’ academic success in public secondary schools in Nyamagana District, Tanzania. The study was guided by the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) theory. The paper adopted a mixed-methods approach using a convergent parallel design. The target population comprised 53,463 respondents, from whom a sample of 201 participants was selected, including 100 students, 92 teachers, 5 heads of schools, 3 Ward Education Officers, and 1 District Secondary Education Officer. Data were collected using questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and direct observation. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics with SPSS version 26, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. title: Applications of artificial intelligence in microbiology education
author: Sherab Pelmo, Vandana Gulati
description: Microbiology underpins understanding of infectious disease, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), biotechnology, public health, food, agriculture and environmental sustainability. Although attention to artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has centred largely on generative tools, a broader range of AI technologies is creating opportunities across microbiology education. This article outlines applications in personalised learning, laboratory skills, diagnostics and image analysis, epidemiology and AMR education, drawing from contemporary literature. It distinguishes microbiology-specific evidence of educational benefit from professional exposure and evidence from other fields and suggests approaches educators can try. Potential benefits include engagement, conceptual understanding, accessibility and professional readiness, alongside challenges such as data privacy, digital inequity, environmental cost and overreliance on AI.

author: Maulidya Ulfah, Sigit Purnama

A correlated three-factor model (AI Use, Learning Perception, and Character Perception) fit better than simpler alternatives and met the tested measurement-invariance criteria. Their contrast was not statistically significant (standardized difference -0.037, CI -0.265 to 0.168), which does not establish group equivalence. title: STUDENT EXPERIENCE OF AI IN LAW ASSESSMENT: AN EXPLORATORY STUDY
author: Benedict Sheehy, Juan Diaz-Granados
description: Legal education faces particular challenges as a result of the wide dissemination of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). GenAI can produce outputs that appear to challenge the work of licensed lawyers. This challenge requires educators and students to be knowledgeable about the powers and limitations of GenAI. This article presents a study of student experimentation with GenAI aimed at developing that knowledge. The experiment incorporated GenAI’s drafting capabilities into an assessment item required in a core subject, Tort Law. The article presents the responses and reflections of the students on the GenAI exercise and provokes further thinking about student experience, uses of and potential with GenAI in legal education. It argues that the most promising pedagogical response is neither blanket prohibition nor uncritical adoption, but a structured use-and-critique model in which students engage directly with GenAI and then evaluate its adequacy against disciplinary and professional standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Influence on Shaping Entrepreneurial Mindsets in Education
author: Anitha Mani, Geetha Manoharan
description: Artificial intelligence is driving significant change in education in general with entrepreneurship included in this research. This research discusses how AI is making a difference in setting the entrepreneurial mindset of students. It explores how AI tools and platforms are increasingly reshaping the way of entrepreneurship is currently taught by providing personalized, interactive and hands-on learning experiences. Incorporating AI powered learning within the curriculum will inculcate an entrepreneurial mindset focusing on creativity, innovation and problem- solving. This research explores case studies of successful AI integration, in which these technologies further enhance the learning process in ultimately better to prepare students for a real-world entrepreneurial challenge. title: AI readiness and indirect associations between AI literacy, TPB-based GAI antecedents, and behavioral intention to use generative AI among undergraduate nursing students: a cross-sectional study
author: Zhaoxu Wang, Jiayi Li
description: Background Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into nursing education. title: From Affordance to Coupling: Reconstructing Foreign Language Pedagogy through an AI-Enabled Production-Oriented Approach
author: Xuan Sun
description: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now a routine presence in foreign language classrooms, yet the gap between what the technology can do and what it actually teaches remains poorly theorised. This paper argues that the gap is structural, and that it is best analysed at the level of the pedagogic move. Taking the Production-Oriented Approach (POA) as its anchor, the paper identifies three chronic constraints in POA practice: the cost of evaluating student output, the difficulty of matching input to diagnosed gaps, and the delay between production and feedback. It then proposes the construct of an AI-enabled Production-Oriented Approach (AI-POA), which frames AI as a change in the resourcing and pacing of an existing cycle. Three affordances of generative AI (generative, dialogic, evaluative) are specified, together with four conditions under which they couple with instruction: goal alignment, temporal placement, cognitive appropriateness and teacher control. description: This study aims to analyze the strategies used in internalizing Love-Based Curriculum values in Akidah Akhlak learning at MTs Cijawura Kota Bandung. A qualitative case study design was employed involving one Akidah Akhlak teacher, one madrasah leader, and five students from Grades VII and VIII. title: Addressing the Youth Suicide Crisis: Policy Recommendations for Schools, Communities, and Health Care Settings
author: Yash K. Garg, Shriya K. Garg
description: About 10% of high school students reported a suicide attempt in 2023, indicating that growing youth suicide rates are an emerging public health crisis. Social and structural factors including trauma, marginalization, and systemic racism contribute to disparities in youth suicide risk and underscore the need to prioritize culturally relevant and responsive crisis intervention. We promote four policy recommendations: (a) placing 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, Crisis Text Line, and local resources on all high school and college student IDs; (b) expanding state-sponsored community and school programs; (c) implementing universal school-based mental health screenings; and (d) promoting lethal means restriction. These policies address critical gaps in current youth suicide prevention approaches.

author: Nur Laila, Alwen Bentri
description: Teaching trigonometric ratios remains challenging because students often struggle with abstract concepts, conventional instruction predominates, and digital learning resources are underused. This study developed a Google Sites learning resource for teaching trigonometric ratios to tenth-grade students at MAS TI Batang Kabung and evaluated its validity and practicality. Data were collected through observations, interviews, documentation, and validation and practicality questionnaires, then analyzed using descriptive quantitative and qualitative techniques. Expert validation scores for content and media were 91.07% and 92.11%, respectively, both classified as highly valid. Practicality scores were 93.42% from the teacher and 86.26% from the students, yielding an overall mean of 89.84%, classified as highly practical. title: Design of a Personalized Learning System for Higher Education Using Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Mobile Technologies
publisher: International Journal of Interactive Mobile Technologies (iJIM)
author: Weijing Li, Tingting Fu
description: Mobile learning in higher education is shifting from ubiquitous access toward contextsensitive personalization. However, cloud-based recommendation systems are constrained by unpredictable latency, insufficient contextual awareness, and limited capacity for continuous adaptation. To address these limitations, an on-device context-adaptive personalization loop (OCAPL) was proposed, in which personalized inference, path generation, and online adaptation were performed directly on mobile devices. The proposed framework was built on three technical pillars: on-device multimodal state inference, context-constrained path generation, and implicit-feedback-driven parameter-efficient updating. Learning behaviors, touch interactions, and device context were jointly integrated. Learning actions were subsequently generated under constraints on latency, energy consumption, memory, and path coherence. Continuous adaptation was further enabled by natural interaction signals and low-rank fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate that OCAPL maintained on-device inference latency below 200 ms, peak memory usage below 50 MB, and additional energy consumption below 5% per hour of learning. title: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF EUROPEAN AND UKRAINIAN FRAMEWORKS GOVERNING THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RESEARCH AND EDUCATION
publisher: INTERNATIONAL CONGRESS FROM RESEARCH TO APPLICATION
author: Nelia KUZNIETSOVA
description: This article presents a comparative analysis of the principal policy and regulatory documents governing the use of generative artificial intelligence in research and higher education. The study examines the European Living Guidelines (third edition, May 2026), the Ukrainian recommendations on the use of artificial intelligence in research (October 2026), and the Ukrainian recommendations for higher education institutions (April 2025). It considers the circumstances that prompted these documents in the context of the emerging concept of postplagiarism, the adoption of Ukraine’s Law on Academic Integrity, and the implementation of the European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act. Using a framework developed for this study and comprising six categories of comparative indicators, the analysis compares the documents’ legal status, target audiences, classifications of AI use and risk assessment criteria, integrity standards and disclosure mechanisms based on the GAIDeT taxonomy, restrictions on the use of AI detection tools, and models of institutional governance. Detailed practical examples illustrate how these frameworks can be implemented in research and education.
